June 23, 2026

 Welcome back to PharmacyInsider.

Today I want to talk about a mineral 

that does not get enough attention 

compared to Vitamin D or Magnesium — 

but is absolutely critical for your 

health.

That mineral is Iron.

And after three years working in a 

pharmacy in Qatar, I can tell you that 

iron deficiency is one of the most 

common problems I see — especially in 

women and people who do not eat enough 

meat.

---

What Exactly Is Iron?

Iron is not a vitamin. It is a mineral.

But it is one of the most important 

minerals your body needs to survive 

and function properly every single day.

The most critical job iron does in your 

body is this — it helps produce Red 

Blood Cells.

Red Blood Cells — also called RBCs — 

are responsible for carrying oxygen 

from your lungs to every single part 

of your body. Your muscles, your brain, 

your organs — everything needs oxygen 

to work.

Without enough iron your body cannot 

make enough Red Blood Cells.

Without enough Red Blood Cells your 

body cannot carry enough oxygen.

Without enough oxygen — everything 

suffers.

This is why iron deficiency makes 

people feel so exhausted even when 

they have done nothing physical.

---

Signs You May Be Iron Deficient

From my daily experience in the 

pharmacy these are the most common 

signs customers come to us with 

before discovering their iron is low:

✓ Constant tiredness and fatigue 

  even after sleeping well

✓ Pale skin — especially noticeable 

  on inner eyelids and palms

✓ Shortness of breath during light 

  activity

✓ Frequent headaches

✓ Cold hands and feet

✓ Brittle nails

✓ Hair fall more than usual

✓ Difficulty concentrating or 

  brain fog

✓ Heart palpitations

If you have three or more of these 

symptoms — please get a blood test 

before buying any supplement. A simple 

CBC blood test confirms iron levels 

in minutes.

---

Who Is Most At Risk

In my pharmacy experience, these 

groups come in most often with iron 

deficiency:

1. Women of reproductive age

Monthly blood loss significantly 

reduces iron levels. This is the 

most common cause of iron deficiency 

I see among female customers.

2. Pregnant women

The baby needs iron to develop 

properly. Pregnant women need almost 

double the normal daily iron intake.

3. Vegetarians and vegans

Iron from plant sources is much 

harder for your body to absorb than 

iron from meat. People who do not 

eat meat need to be extra careful 

about their iron intake.

4. People doing heavy physical work

Intense physical activity increases 

iron requirements. Many manual 

workers in Qatar are at higher risk 

of iron deficiency without knowing.

5. People who donate blood regularly

Each blood donation removes iron 

from your body. Frequent donors 

must monitor their iron levels.

---

Two Types of Iron You Need to Know

This is something I explain to 

customers regularly because it 

affects how well your supplement 

actually works.

Type 1 — Heme Iron

Found in animal products — red meat, 

chicken, fish. Your body absorbs 

this type very efficiently — up to 

30% absorption rate.

Type 2 — Non-Heme Iron

Found in plant sources — spinach, 

lentils, beans, fortified cereals. 

Your body absorbs this much less 

efficiently — only 2 to 10%.

This is why vegetarians need to 

consume significantly more iron 

rich foods than meat eaters to 

reach the same iron levels.

---

Iron Supplements — What I Tell 

Customers

When customers ask about iron 

supplements I always tell them 

the same four things:

1. Get tested first

Never start iron supplements 

without a blood test. Too much 

iron is also dangerous — a 

condition called Iron Overload 

or Hemochromatosis. More is 

not always better.

2. Take with Vitamin C

Vitamin C dramatically increases 

iron absorption. Take your iron 

supplement with a glass of orange 

juice or a Vitamin C supplement 

for best results.

3. Do not take with dairy or coffee

Calcium in dairy and compounds 

in coffee and tea block iron 

absorption significantly. Take 

iron at least 2 hours away from 

these.

4. Expect digestive side effects

Iron supplements commonly cause 

constipation, nausea, or dark 

stools. This is normal and not 

dangerous. If side effects are 

severe speak to your doctor about 

a gentler iron form.

---

Important Warning

Iron supplements are one of the 

leading causes of poisoning in 

young children. Never leave iron 

supplements where children can 

reach them.

Additionally — never give adult 

iron supplements to children 

without direct medical supervision.

---

My Honest Pharmacy Observation

Iron deficiency is genuinely one 

of the most underdiagnosed 

conditions I see. So many customers 

come in buying energy drinks and 

caffeine products when what they 

actually need is a simple iron 

blood test.

If you have been feeling exhausted 

for weeks with no clear reason — 

please get a blood test before 

spending money on supplements.

A simple test costs very little. 

The results will tell you exactly 

what your body needs.

 on Amazon"

---

DISCLAIMER:

I am a pharmacy assistant not a 

licensed pharmacist or doctor. 

This content is for informational 

purposes only. Always consult a 

qualified healthcare professional 

before starting iron supplements 

especially during pregnancy or 

for children.
